position: Current Regulations That Should Be Rolled Back (Civil Rights Data Collection)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department rescind the Biden-era changes to the Civil Rights Data Collection that added a nonbinary sex category and retired data on high school single-sex athletics sports, teams and participants. It also recommends issuing a new CRDC that collects data directly relevant to the Office for Civil Rights' statutory enforcement authority.
remaining: Confirmation that the single-sex athletics items (sports, teams and participants by sex) are in the approved collection.
Any statement or redesign showing the CRDC is limited to data tied to OCR's statutory enforcement authority, which the Mandate also asks for.
Fielding of the 2027-28 collection under the approved instrument.

status_summary: ED submitted a revised Civil Rights Data Collection for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 school years to OMB, with a 30-day notice published 2025-08-07 (comments closed 2025-09-08). OMB's reginfo.gov record shows the revision (OMB control number 1870-0504) approved with change on 2026-07-20, with an expiration of 2029-07-31. According to K-12 Dive on 2026-07-31, the approved collection drops the nonbinary category, so schools report students as male or female, and removes gender identity from the rape and sexual assault definitions, with ED citing costs outweighing benefits and Executive Order 14168. Whether the single-sex athletics items are in the approved collection was not confirmed, and no ED statement tying the collection to OCR's statutory enforcement authority, as the Mandate asks, was located; the stage rests on the removal of the nonbinary category, which is the change the text names.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14168 was signed, setting a federal policy of recognizing two sexes, male and female; ED later cited it in explaining the CRDC changes, per K-12 Dive.

ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act 30-day notice submitting a revised CRDC (OMB control number 1870-0504, docket ED-2024-SCC-0128) for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 collections; comments closed 2025-09-08.
K-12 Dive reported that the proposal would stop collecting data on nonbinary and transgender students and remove gender identity from the rape definition, as aligned with the 2020 Title IX rule.
OMB concluded its review of the revised CRDC information collection as approved with change, with an expiration date of 2029-07-31.
timeline.source: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (reginfo.gov)

timeline.event: K-12 Dive reported that the approved 2025-26 collection drops the nonbinary category and gender identity wording in the rape and sexual assault definitions, and that districts that had recorded nonbinary students must recode them as male or female.

title: Drop the CRDC nonbinary category, keep athletics data, refocus CRDC on OCR enforcement
uncertainties: The Federal Register notice and the reginfo.gov ICR page do not list individual data elements; the specific changes (nonbinary category, rape and sexual assault definitions) come from K-12 Dive reporting and from a multistate attorneys general comment letter on the proposal (oag.ca.gov), while the supporting statement and the 30-day comment response posted on reginfo.gov on 2026-07-16 could not be opened (no document links were readable, and regulations.gov could not be reached). The reginfo.gov page shows the approval date 2026-07-20 and an approval with change, but no terms of clearance text. No source read in this review mentions athletics in the 2025-26 proposal or approval: the K-12 Dive, EdSurge and multistate letter coverage is silent on it. A vendor help page (kb.infinitecampus.com) shows the single-sex athletics questions (ATHL-2, ATHL-3) in the 2021-22 collection, which suggests the retirement the Mandate objected to may not have taken effect, but this was not confirmed from ED documents. EdSurge (2025-10-06) also reported removal of some state-level discipline disproportionality data, which is outside this recommendation. The Mandate refers to the December 2021 notice for the 2021-22 collection.
